## What to change {#act1-fix}

::: {.beforeafter}
::: {}
[The sentence]{.label}
"Explains" and "cause" claim a direction the code never tested. For Demo A, r = −0.57 falls to 0.14 once both seasonal trends are removed: r² drops from 32 % to 2 %. The season moved both.
:::
::: {}
[A sentence the data allow]{.label}
"From 20 June to 9 October 2004, cooler days had more NOx (r = −0.57, 77 days). After removing each series' 29-day trend, r = 0.14. Most of the association follows the season."
:::
:::

[Before any sentence: plot both series over time, then remove what they share.]{.note-line}

    g += ticks.map((v) => `<line x1="${L}" x2="${W - R}" y1="${V(v)}" y2="${V(v)}" stroke="#B9C1C6"/><text x="${L - 10}" y="${V(v) + 6}" text-anchor="end" font-size="17" fill="#333F4A">${mn(v)}</text>`).join('');
    for (let k = 0; k < n; k += 14) g += `<text x="${X(k)}" y="${H - B + 24}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" fill="#333F4A">${D.dates[k]}</text>`;

'stroke-dasharray="7 5"' : ''}/><text x="${left ? X(k) - 7 : X(k) + 7}" y="${T + dy}" text-anchor="${left ? 'end' : 'start'}" font-size="18" font-weight="700" fill="${color}">${text}</text>`;

    let g, V;

      let d = ''; D.up.forEach((u, k) => { d += (k ? 'L' : 'M') + X(k).toFixed(1) + ',' + V(Math.min(u, 60)).toFixed(1); });
      g += `<clipPath id="dr-clip"><rect x="${L}" y="${T}" width="${W - L - R}" height="${H - T - B}"/></clipPath><path d="${d}" fill="none" stroke="#E29A2D" stroke-width="3.5" clip-path="url(#dr-clip)"/>`;
      g += vline(D.onset, '#9a5f10', true, 'start: ' + D.dates[D.onset], 60, true) + vline(D.alarm, '#9a5f10', false, 'alarm: ' + D.dates[D.alarm], 60);
      g += `<text x="${W - R - 6}" y="${T + 22}" text-anchor="end" font-size="16" fill="#66727C">sum leaves the top of the chart; it reaches ${Math.round(Math.max(...D.up))} by 20/07</text>`;
    } else {
      [g, V] = axes(-6, 10, [-5, 0, 5, 10], 'benzene minus sensor, µg/m³');
      g += `<line x1="${L}" x2="${W - R}" y1="${V(D.mu)}" y2="${V(D.mu)}" stroke="#333F4A" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-dasharray="4 4"/>`;
      if (v === 'thr') {
        for (const s of [-3, 3]) g += `<line x1="${L}" x2="${W - R}" y1="${V(D.mu + s * D.sigma)}" y2="${V(D.mu + s * D.sigma)}" stroke="#333F4A" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="7 5"/>`;
        g += `<text x="${W - R - 6}" y="${V(D.mu + 3 * D.sigma) - 8}" text-anchor="end" font-size="17" fill="#333F4A">mean + 3σ</text>`;
        g += vline(D.thr, '#BE654C', false, '3σ alarm: ' + D.dates[D.thr], 26);
      }
      D.res.forEach((r, k) => { if (r === null) return; g += k < CAL ? `<circle cx="${X(k)}" cy="${V(r)}" r="6" fill="#fff" stroke="#0F6E6B" stroke-width="2.5"/>` : `<circle cx="${X(k)}" cy="${V(r)}" r="6" fill="${v === 'thr' && k === D.thr ? '#BE654C' : '#0F6E6B'}"/>`; });
    }
    document.getElementById('dr-plot').innerHTML = g;
    document.getElementById('dr-out').textContent = {
      res: 'Each point is one day: benzene from the analyzer minus the benzene the calibrated sensor predicts. Open points: the 14 calibration days, mean ' + D.mu + ', σ = ' + D.sigma + '.',
      thr: 'The 3σ rule waits for one day beyond mean + 3σ (5.27). That day is ' + D.dates[D.thr] + ', day ' + (D.thr + 1) + '. The points had been high for three weeks.',
      cus: 'CUSUM adds each day’s excess over the mean, minus an allowance k = 0.5σ, and never goes below zero. It passes h on ' + D.dates[D.alarm] + ' (day ' + (D.alarm + 1) + '); it last stood at zero on ' + D.dates[D.onset - 1] + ', so the estimated start is ' + D.dates[D.onset] + '.',
    }[v];
    root.querySelectorAll('[data-v]').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', b.dataset.v === v));
  }
  root.querySelectorAll('[data-v]').forEach((b) => b.addEventListener('click', () => draw(b.dataset.v)));
  draw('res');
})();
</script>

## How CUSUM adds up {#cusum-steps}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
| Day | Date | Difference | minus mean, minus k | Running sum |
|:--|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| 15 | 14/04 | 1.64 | 0.75 | 0.75 |
| 16 | 15/04 | 0.94 | 0.05 | 0.80 |
| 17 | 16/04 | −0.41 | −1.30 | 0.00 |
| 18 | 17/04 | −0.04 | −0.93 | 0.00 |
| 19 | 18/04 | −0.68 | −1.57 | 0.00 |
| 20 | 19/04 | 1.58 | 0.69 | 0.69 |
| 21 | 20/04 | 4.17 | 3.28 | 3.97 |
| 22 | 21/04 | 4.87 | 3.98 | 7.95 |
| 23 | 22/04 | 5.02 | 4.13 | **12.08** |
| 24 | 23/04 | 3.93 | 3.04 | 15.12 |
:::
::: {.column width="38%"}
::: {.calc-note}
Mean of the calibration days 0.02, σ = 1.7486 µg/m³ (about 1.75).

Allowance k = 0.5σ = 0.87. Limit h = 5σ = 8.74.

Sum = max(0, previous sum + difference − mean − k).

The sum passes h on day 23. The last day it was zero, day 19, marks the estimated start: day 20.
:::
:::
::::

[A second sum does the same for differences below the mean. The sums here use the rounded numbers shown, so you can check them by hand; the lab uses full precision, and its sums can differ by 0.01. The alarm day is the same.]{.note-line}

## Two rules, one drift {#two-rules}

::: {.checks3}
::: {.c4}
[[3σ]{.nocap} rule]{.label}
Alarms on one day far from the mean. Good for a sudden step. For Demo A: day 41, three weeks after the drift began.
:::
::: {.c4}
[CUSUM]{.label}
Adds small differences that keep the same sign. Good for a slow drift. For Demo A: alarm day 23, estimated start day 20.
:::
::: {.c4}
[The cost]{.label}
A smaller k or h alarms sooner, and also alarms more often on noise. The Extension view, Step 9, lets you try.
:::
:::

[Both rules need a calibration period that was in control. If the sensor had already drifted then, neither rule can see it.]{.note-line}
